Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
656 AM EST Mon Nov 23 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
No significant changes.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Unseasonably warm conditions continue today before much 
cooler weather returns Tuesday and Wednesday.

2) A coastal storm system will likely impact the area Thursday 
into a portion of Friday with rain, strong gusty winds, and 
widespread coastal flooding.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
Dry conditions are expected through Wednesday. A cold front 
will move across the area this afternoon, but temperatures will 
remain well above normal in the 60s. Most of the record highs 
are around 70. KISP has tied or broken its high temperature 
record the last 4 days. It seems unlikely this will happen again
today. See climate section below for November 23 record highs.


Much cooler weather will be on tap for Tuesday and Wednesday as an 
anomalously (2-3SD+) strong area of high pressure (1040+ mb) builds 
from the Great Lakes into the Northeast. Daytimes high will struggle 
to get out of the 40s with lows manly below freezing except NYC 
metro Wednesday morning.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Confidence continues that a much larger scale coastal storm
system will impact the area Thursday into Friday with rain, 
strong wind gusts, and widespread coastal flooding. 

This is looking to be a very different system compared to the
one that just passed by Sunday night. The aforementioned 
anomalously strong surface high over the northeast will give way
to a broad area of low pressure tracking north along the 
eastern seaboard. There continues to be signals that the low may
track inland from the coast to along or just west of the spine 
of the Appalachians. Regardless, a strong pressure gradient will
be in place between the departing high and approaching storm 
system. 

The timing has slowed down a bit in the latest model consensus
with easterly winds beginning to ramp up late Wednesday night, 
but especially Thanksgiving morning. The highest probability of 
rain may also occur Thanksgiving afternoon into the nighttime, 
with the immediate coast standing the highest chance of some 
rain in the morning. The rain likely begins tapering off early 
Friday morning.

A consensus forecast right now produces ENE winds of 20 to 30 mph 
with gusts 35 to 45 mph, possibly even around 50 mph at the coast. 
The strongest winds look to occur in the afternoon and evening 
before a gradual weakening at night. The NBM probability for 
exceeding 45 mph wind gusts (advisory level) is about 50-70 percent 
along the coast and much lower inland. The storm departs to the 
north and east on Friday but there still may be W gusts 25-35 mph.

Potential total rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches look reasonable
at this time. The NBM probability of exceeding 2.5 inches is 
about 20 to 30 percent near the coast, and has remained similar 
for the past few runs. These amounts may occur over a 12-18 
period. Freshwater flooding impacts look limited to minor urban 
and poor drainage due to the progressive nature of the system. 

Coastal flooding is also growing more likely with a full moon on
the 24th and king tides this week. Many locations need less 
than a foot to reach minor coastal flood benchmarks. The current
forecast supports widespread minor to moderate flooding. 
Localized major is a possibility for the most vulnerable 
locations of the south shore back bays and western Great South 
Bay. In addition beach flooding, erosion, and overwash would all
be on the table.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z MONDAY THROUGH FRIDAY/...
A cold front moves across the terminals this afternoon, with 
high pressure building in behind it.

Conditions continue to improve with most terminals VFR with 
some pockets of MVFR. Expect VFR conditions to prevail through
the remainder of the TAF period. 

Winds will generally be from the W today. Winds become more NW
later this afternoon behind a cold front. Expect some gusts to 
15-20 kt behind the frontal passage. 


 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

Timing of wind gusts may be off by an hour or two. 

.OUTLOOK FOR 12Z Tuesday through Friday... 

Tuesday: VFR. NW winds 10-15 kt with gusts up to 20 kt. 

Late Tuesday night and Wednesday: VFR. 

Wednesday night: MVFR cigs developing with slight chance of rain 
late. Increasing E-NE winds with gusts 20-30 kt, highest in the 
NYC metro area and along the coast. 

Thursday: Rain with IFR cond. E-NE winds gusting to 35-45 kt,
highest in the NYC metro area and along the coast. 

Friday: Still a chance of rain mainly in the morning, with
flight cat improving to MVFR. W winds gusting to 25-30 kt. 

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component
forecasts, can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
SCA conditions will continue today, mainly in seas, on the
nearshore ocean waters and the LI Sound east of the CT River. 
Seas should subside tonight into Tuesday, but may linger around 
5 ft on the nearshore ocean through early Tuesday afternoon. 
High pressure building in on Tuesday may bring a period of 
marginal SCA gusts.

A lull in SCA conditions is expected late Tuesday into Wednesday 
before conditions start to ramp up Wednesday night ahead of an 
approaching low pressure from the south. Gale conditions are likely 
with potential of storm force on Thursday and Thursday evening. Max 
significant wave heights should ramp up to 15-20 ft on the ocean and 
occasionally to 20-25 ft out east, 7-10 ft across LI Sound and 
around 10 ft on western Block Island Sound E of Orient Point. Gales 
may continue into Friday as the storm departs to the north.
